facts.raw_span: 5-year history of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque
no previous history of trauma or any other systemic symptoms
nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
No local lymphadenopathy was observed
Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
HIV: Negative
Hepatitis B: Negative
Hepatitis C: Negative
Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Perls Prussian blue staining showed prominent hemosiderin deposits

support_spans: Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
Negative for human herpesvirus 8 (HHV-8) and Wilms tumor 1 (WT1)
concepts.why: The presence of vascular channel endothelial cells positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40, along with the negative results for HHV-8 and WT1, supports the diagnosis of Kaposi's sarcoma, although the negative HIV status is unexpected.

support_spans: Poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation
Perls Prussian blue staining showed prominent hemosiderin deposits
contradict_spans: Vascular channel endothelial cells were positive for CD31, CD34, and D2-40
concepts.why: The presence of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation and prominent hemosiderin deposits supports the diagnosis of Hemangioma, although the positive results for CD31, CD34, and D2-40 are more typical of other vascular tumors.

support_spans: nonindurated and well-defined 10 × 8-cm reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis
Ki-67 index showed low proliferation in endothelial cells
contradict_spans: No cellular pleomorphism, mitotic figures, or intravascular red blood cells
concepts.why: The presence of a nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis and a low Ki-67 index supports the diagnosis of Angiosarcoma, although the lack of cellular pleomorphism and mitotic figures is unexpected.

The patient's presentation of an asymptomatic, gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border and the histologic findings of poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation with hemosiderin deposits are consistent with Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma.

rationales.F01: The presence of a gradually enlarging, reddish hematomalike plaque is more typical of Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma.
rationales.F03: The nonindurated and well-defined reddish-brown annular plaque with peripheral ecchymosis is more characteristic of Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma.
rationales.F05: The positivity for CD31, CD34, and D2-40 is common in various vascular tumors, including Hemangioma and Angiosarcoma.
rationales.F06: The absence of HHV-8 and WT1 helps to rule out Kaposi's sarcoma.
rationales.F07: The low proliferation index in endothelial cells makes Angiosarcoma less likely.
rationales.F11: The poorly defined, superficial, and deep dermal vascular proliferation is seen in various vascular tumors.
rationales.F12: The presence of prominent hemosiderin deposits is characteristic of Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma.

frontier_selector.why: The presence of a reddish hematomalike plaque with a brownish peripheral border and prominent hemosiderin deposits, along with the characteristic promontory signs, are highly suggestive of Targetoid Hemosiderotic Hemangioma.
